newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FCC denies stay request of phone charge rules.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FCC denies stay request of phone charge rules.

text.p: The Federal Communications Commission Wednesday denied a request by SBC Communications Inc and GTE Corp to suspend key portions of its recent overhaul of domestic phone charges.
The agency, in a release, said the two carriers had "failed to show that they are entitled to the relief they have requested."
The FCC last month ordered an immediate cut of $1.7 billion from the $23 billion a year long-distance carriers pay local carriers to connect calls as part of its overhaul of domestic phone charges.
SBC -- the first carrier to seek a stay -- argued that the FCC went too far in requiring the access charge reductions, which are expected to total $18.5 billion over five years.
The carrier also complained the rules would let competitors lease parts of the local network -- such as call-switching devices -- without paying access charges.
But the FCC, in rejecting the stay request, said the new rules "will lead to lower long-distance rates for consumers, which should cause long-distance calling to increase."
SBC has asked a U.S. appeals court in St. Louis to suspend the rules and the carrier plans to ask the court to stay the rules while it considers the case.
